platform.name: QuickKart
platform.kind: quick-commerce grocery e-commerce with KartPlus membership
platform.summary: Online grocery store with product listings, cart, checkout and payment, a ₹99/month KartPlus membership with a 14-day trial, and sponsored and creator-promoted products.

rules.title: No false urgency or false scarcity
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 1 (False Urgency); CPA 2019 s.2(47); see also ASCI deceptive-design Guideline 3 (advertiser must substantiate stock level behind scarcity claims)
rules.explanation: Every product card shows a random 'Only N left' count. The product page 'Deal ends in' timer restarts at a random 9–14 minutes on each load, so neither is tied to real stock or a real offer end date.
rules.recommendation: Show stock only from real inventory data, and drive the timer from the server-side offerEndsAt date. Remove both when there is no real data behind them.

rules.title: No items, services, donations or charges added to the basket without consent
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 2 (Basket Sneaking), incl. proviso for free samples, complimentary services and disclosed necessary fees
rules.explanation: The cart opens with the paid QuickProtect add-on (₹19) and the ₹2 donation already ticked and added to the total.
rules.recommendation: Start both add-ons as useState(false). Add them to the bill only after the user ticks them.

rules.title: No confirm shaming in decline or opt-out copy
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 3 (Confirm Shaming)
rules.explanation: Decline and close options use neutral wording ('Not now') and carry no guilt or fear messaging.

rules.title: No forced action to get the intended product
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 4 (Forced Action)

evidence.snippet: Checkout as guest or sign in.

rules.explanation: Guest checkout is available, and no unneeded sign-up or item is required to buy.

rules.title: Cancelling a subscription is simple, visible and clear
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 5 (Subscription Trap), sub-items (i) to (iv)

evidence.snippet: To cancel KartPlus, call our membership desk on 1800 266 9090 (Mon–Fri, 10 am – 6 pm). Cancellation requests by email or chat are not accepted.

rules.explanation: There is no cancel button. Cancelling takes a phone call within limited hours, while sign-up is a single click.
rules.recommendation: Add a clearly labelled 'Cancel subscription' button in Account → KartPlus that cancels in one or two steps with a confirmation.

elements.text: To cancel, call 1800 266 9090 (Mon–Fri, 10–6). Email/chat not accepted.

rules.title: No interface interference that highlights one choice and hides another
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 6 (Interface Interference)
rules.explanation: The close icon only dismisses the prompt, and the membership page gives 'Start trial' and 'Not now' comparable button weight.

rules.title: No bait and switch
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 7 (Bait and Switch)

evidence.snippet: Price comes from the catalogue at the moment of adding and never changes inside the cart.

rules.explanation: The cart uses the listing's own id and price, with no substitution.

rules.title: No drip pricing: the full price is shown upfront
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 8 (Drip Pricing), (i) to (iv)
rules.explanation: The mandatory ₹9 platform fee and ₹19 handling fee are left out of the cart and checkout totals. They appear only at the payment step, so the payable amount rises by ₹28.
rules.recommendation: Show every mandatory fee in the price from the cart onward, or include them in the displayed price.

rules.title: Advertising is not disguised as other content
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 9 (Disguised Advertisement); CCPA Misleading Advertisements Guidelines, 2022

evidence.snippet: <a href=... className="card tile"> (no Sponsored badge rendered)

rules.explanation: Sponsored products are placed first under 'Top picks for you' and use the same card as organic items, with no label. The creator picks do carry a 'Paid partnership' badge.
rules.recommendation: Render a visible 'Sponsored' badge on ProductCard when p.sponsored is true.

elements.text: Assam CTC Tea 500 g (paid placement, shown first)

rules.title: No nagging
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 10 (Nagging)
rules.explanation: The newsletter prompt respects a stored dismissal.

rules.title: No trick questions or confusing wording
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 11 (Trick Question)

evidence.snippet: <input type="checkbox" defaultChecked /> Uncheck this box if you do not wish to not receive offers

rules.explanation: The checkbox is ticked by default and uses a double negative ('do not wish to not receive'). Its meaning is inverted compared with the sibling opt-in boxes.
rules.recommendation: Replace it with an unticked box labelled 'Send me offers' that follows the same checked-means-yes rule as the others.

elements.text: Uncheck this box if you do not wish to not receive offers and messages from QuickKart and its partners.

rules.title: No surreptitious SaaS billing
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 12 (SaaS Billing)

evidence.snippet: After that ₹99 is charged on the same date each month until you cancel. We send a reminder 3 days before the first charge

rules.explanation: The plan screen states the trial length, amount, frequency and reminders next to the sign-up button. This is judged from the copy only, because no reminder job exists in the code.

rules.title: No rogue malware or scareware
rules.source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, Annexure 1 item 13 (Rogue Malwares)
rules.explanation: The platform sells no security products and shows no device alerts.

rules.title: 'Free' claims disclose every condition
rules.source: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 s.2(28) (misleading advertisement); CCPA Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements, 2022 (free claims); PhysicsWallah order (PIB, 3 Jun 2026)

evidence.snippet: Free for the first 14 days. After that ₹99 is charged...

rules.explanation: The free-trial claim is accompanied by the later charge and the mandate requirement in the same view.

rules.title: Purchase consent only by explicit affirmative action; no pre-ticked boxes
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(9)
rules.explanation: The protection and donation purchase options are pre-selected, so consent to pay is assumed.
rules.recommendation: Default both to false and record consent only on a click.

rules.title: Entity identity, customer care and grievance officer shown on the platform
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(2) and 4(4); Rule 6(5)(e) for sellers; DPDP Act s.6(3) contact person (data requests)
rules.explanation: The footer shows the legal name, address, customer care and grievance officer. The account privacy page lists a data-protection contact.

rules.title: Total price in a single figure with a breakup of all charges
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 6(5)(b) (marketplace sellers) and Rule 7(1)(e) (inventory entities); Rule 5(3)(e)
rules.explanation: The payment step lists each charge line and a total equal to their sum. The late appearance of the fees is covered under drip pricing.

rules.title: Return, refund, exchange, warranty, delivery and payment info shown pre-purchase
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 5(3)(c), 6(5)(g)-(i), 7(1)(a); best-before date added by E-Commerce (Amendment) Rules, 2026 from 1 Jan 2027

evidence.snippet: Returns: unopened packaged items can be returned within 7 days for a full refund. <a href="/policies/returns">

rules.explanation: The product page shows the return terms, links the return policy and shows the delivery time.

rules.title: Payment methods, fees and how to cancel regular payments disclosed
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 5(3)(d) and Rule 7(1)(c)

evidence.snippet: No payment method carries an extra fee. ... to stop recurring payments, call our membership desk

rules.explanation: Payment methods, the absence of method fees and the procedure to stop autopay are all disclosed, even though the procedure is a phone call.

rules.title: Seller details shown on marketplace listings
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 5(3)(a); seller website/email added by 2026 Amendment from 1 Jan 2027
rules.explanation: Seller name, address and rating are shown on the product page.

rules.title: Importer and country of origin shown for imported goods
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(6) and 6(5)(d),(f); Rule 4(6)(b) as amended 2026 (from 1 Jan 2027)
rules.explanation: Country of origin and importer are rendered on the product page.

rules.title: No price discrimination between consumers of the same class
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(11)(a)-(b); CCPA notices to Ola/Uber on device-based fares (Jan 2025)
rules.explanation: Price calculation uses no device, OS or user-agent inputs.

rules.title: Ranking parameters disclosed; search not manipulated
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 5(3)(f) (descending order from 2027) and Rule 4(11)(c) inserted by 2026 Amendment (from 1 Jan 2027)
rules.explanation: A ranking policy page exists and links from search. The ranking code uses relevance, rating and delivery speed with no paid boost.

rules.title: Sponsored listings distinctly and prominently labelled
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, new Rule 4(12) (notified 9 Sep 2026, in force 1 Jan 2027)

evidence.snippet: card renders no use of p.sponsored

rules.explanation: The sponsored flag moves products to the top of the home listing, but the card never shows a 'Sponsored' label.
rules.recommendation: Show a readable 'Sponsored' badge on cards where p.sponsored is true.

rules.title: Discounts show the prior price (lowest in the previous 30 days)
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, new Rule 4(13) (in force 1 Jan 2027)

evidence.snippet: Lowest price in the 30 days before the current offer. lowest30d
Lowest price in the last 30 days: ₹{p.lowest30d}

rules.explanation: The lowest 30-day price is stored per product and displayed next to the price.

rules.title: Dark-pattern self-audit certificate displayed
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, new Rule 4(15) (in force 1 Jan 2027); CCPA advisory of 5 Jun 2025
rules.explanation: The footer links to a self-audit certificate.

rules.title: No bundled fees for unrelated services
rules.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, new Rule 5(7) (in force 1 Jan 2027); exception for loyalty/membership programmes
rules.explanation: The platform fee covers only platform services. Protection and donation are separate lines.

rules.title: Consent requests come with a clear, standalone notice
rules.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.5(1) and s.6(3); DPDP Rules, 2025 Rule 3 (in force 18 months after 14 Nov 2025)

evidence.snippet: We collect your name, phone and delivery address ... withdraw ... Full privacy notice (English, हिन्दी, ಕನ್ನಡ)

rules.explanation: A standalone notice at sign-up lists the data, the purposes, how to withdraw and the available languages.

rules.title: Data consent by clear affirmative action; no pre-ticked consent
rules.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.6(1)

evidence.snippet: <input type="checkbox" defaultChecked /> Uncheck this box if you do not wish to not receive offers

rules.explanation: The marketing consent (offers from QuickKart and partners) is pre-ticked at sign-up. The other purposes default to off.
rules.recommendation: Make the marketing box unticked and record consent only after a click.

elements.text: Uncheck this box if you do not wish to not receive offers and messages from QuickKart and its partners.

rules.title: Consent is specific, unbundled and not a condition for unnecessary data
rules.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.6(1) (free, specific, unconditional; limited to necessary data) and its telemedicine illustration

evidence.snippet: orders required; offers_email, offers_sms, personalised separate

rules.explanation: Each optional purpose has its own choice, and the core service needs only the data required for delivery.

rules.title: Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it
rules.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.6(4); DPDP Rules, 2025 Rule 3(c)(i)
rules.explanation: Account → Privacy has a one-click toggle for each optional consent.

rules.title: Children: verifiable parental consent; no tracking or targeted ads
rules.source: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.9(1) and 9(3); DPDP Rules, 2025 Rule 10

evidence.snippet: You must be 18 or older to create an account.

rules.explanation: This is a grocery platform not directed at children, and its sign-up states an 18+ requirement.

rules.title: Recurring payments set up only through a disclosed, authenticated mandate
rules.source: RBI Digital Payments - E-mandate Framework, 2026 (21 Apr 2026), paras 4(a)-(c), 5(a), 8 (issuer/acquirer duties; acquirers must ensure merchant compliance, para 10(c))

evidence.snippet: max ₹99 per debit, valid 12 months. You approve the mandate with your UPI PIN or card OTP.

rules.explanation: The mandate screen shows the cap, frequency and validity, and requires authentication. This is judged from the copy only, as no gateway code is present.

rules.title: Users can see and withdraw a mandate; renewal is notified
rules.source: RBI Digital Payments - E-mandate Framework, 2026 (21 Apr 2026), paras 4(b) (withdraw at any time, communicated at registration), 6 (24-hour pre-debit notification and opt-out)

evidence.snippet: To cancel KartPlus, call our membership desk on 1800 266 9090

rules.explanation: The account page shows the plan but has no mandate view or revoke action. Withdrawal is possible only by phone.
rules.recommendation: Add an in-app control that lists active mandates and revokes them through the gateway, and say at registration that the mandate can be withdrawn.

rules.title: Tips only after the service; no pay-more prompts during booking
rules.source: Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025 (tipping only after ride, as cited by CCPA); CCPA Rapido order (PIB, 15 Sep 2026)
rules.explanation: There is no ride-hailing or tipping flow.

rules.title: Advertised and listed prices include non-optional fees
rules.source: ASCI Guidelines for Online Deceptive Design Patterns in Advertising (15 Jun 2023, applicable from 1 Sep 2023), Guideline 1 (Drip Pricing)

evidence.snippet: Platform and handling fees apply to every order

rules.explanation: Listing prices exclude the platform and handling fees that every buyer pays later.
rules.recommendation: Disclose the platform and handling fees alongside listing prices, or fold them into the price.

rules.title: Ad symbols keep their usual meaning (X closes)
rules.source: ASCI Guidelines for Online Deceptive Design Patterns in Advertising (15 Jun 2023, applicable from 1 Sep 2023), Guideline 2 (Bait and Switch), example (c)
rules.explanation: The close control only dismisses the prompt.

rules.title: Influencer, paid-review and editorial-style ads are labelled
rules.source: ASCI Guidelines for Online Deceptive Design Patterns in Advertising (15 Jun 2023, applicable from 1 Sep 2023), Guideline 4 (Disguised Ads; numbered DD-3 here because ASCI Guideline 3 is folded into CCPA-DP-01); ASCI influencer advertising guidelines
rules.explanation: Paid creator picks show a 'Paid partnership' label.

rules.title: Mandatory packaged-commodity declarations shown on product pages
rules.source: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011, Rule 6(10) (inserted 2017, effective 1 Jan 2018) read with Rule 6(1)

evidence.snippet: Generic name, Net quantity, Unit sale price, Manufacturer, Country of origin, Consumer care

rules.explanation: The product page renders the Rule 6(1) declarations, with MRP and the manufacture and best-before dates.

rules.title: Searchable, sortable country-of-origin filter for imported goods
rules.source: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Amendment Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 128(E) of 13 Feb 2026, new Rule 6(10A) (reported in force 1 Jul 2026)
rules.explanation: Search offers a country-of-origin filter backed by the product field.
